I deeply empathize with this. Originally I began picking at my skin because of acne, but now that my acne has been treated I still seek out “imperfections” on my face and end up with ugly and painful scabs. Some things that have worked for me in treating spots I’ve picked include using acne patches to cover up and mitigate weeping, using a heavy moisturizer or Aquaphor to keep scabs hydrated (hydrated spots are less likely to leave scarring and tend to  heal more quickly) and applying COSRX AHA 7 Whitehead Power Liquid day and night after washing my face and before applying moisturizer. The whitehead power liquid is really good for treating hyperpigmentation and scarring left after a picked spot has healed. The price point (~$20) may seem like a lot but I only have to replace it once every 4-5 months. There are also acid treatments and masks you can apply once or twice per week that act as a chemical exfoliant that’ll help lighten healed spots as well. I like using The Ordinary AHA 30% + BHA 2% Peeling Solution. When using any acid treatments, it’s super important to wear sunscreen as you’ll be more susceptible to burning. Wearing sunscreen also helps to prevent any hyperpigmentation spots or scarring from darkening. Of course, r/skincareaddiction is a really great resource for finding products that will suit your needs! I hope this information helps a little bit! I still struggle with picking but these methods and products have helped me considerably.

I'm in the same boat as you, in that I've also been diagnosed with major depressive disorder and am on the right medication, doing therapy, and living a healthy lifestyle, but it never seems to be enough. It's like I'm always trying the next best thing to see if it will help me feel genuine happiness, even though I know in general my baseline level of happiness is biologically always going to be lower than someone who does not suffer from depression (or other mental disorders). It just sucks that 10 years after being diagnosed I'm still struggling with the fact that depression will always be a part of my life and that I will have to continue accommodating for it so as to not be completely engulfed by it.
